comments.text: The trouble with "emergence" is that we don’t know if the architectures that have been developed are sufficiently rich enough to allow intelligence to emerge. Hypothetically, you might think that simply simulating biological neurons and training them would result in human-level intelligence emerging. However, the reality is far from this. Initially, we had to utilize backpropagation (for which there isn’t a good biological analogy), and since we can’t simulate the highly recursive and parallel capabilities of biological neurons, we’ve had to develop architectures that approximate these mechanisms, such as attention (which simplifies RNN-based models approach to recursion). The question stands, do we need to improve the acitecture to encapsulate another subtle feature of intelligence, or do we just say with fingers crossed, emergence will solve it this time for sure?

Here's a simple question. This comes from my own experience. Let's say I work with lots of numerical data, think databases of numeric data, millions of rows of data with 100's of columns across multiple tables. Why would I spend time "distilling" an LLM to teach it to run analysis, when I can simply run a GLM, or xgboost model, or multiple other well understood statistical models to give me the same thing. 
I'm calling BS. I work with data, I have tried a lot of models, and the only use case I have found is me walking A LLM through each step of the analysis to get me what I am looking for, any time I let any of these models try to do the full analysis, they are smoking crack. The hallucinations thing is a big deal when dealing with statistical data. It just needs to hallucinate 1 line of code, and BAM the whole analysis is wrong. 
When dealing with data with both numerical and dimensional data, I find a random forest derivative far better than anything ANY of these LLM's have given ()unless it codes a random forest derivative). The upside of a random forest derivative model is I can understand it. Yes sometimes a neural net is better, but for what I do, known model are better.  

We've been here before, I don't care that openAI has been given billions of dollars, we are still asking the same basic question, and those that understand basic calculus, can clearly see, we haven't moved forward in the realm of numeric data analysis at all. This is my reason for being bearish LLM's they do not have capabilities for deep numerical analysis
